overall: A person who has stood in a pasture with a sick calf telling you what is coming up from the border, dry and unhurried, never selling the technology. The read starts level and informed, rises slightly for the personal stretch with Bellinger, drops to its quietest at the sterile fly numbers and the producer instruction, and lands low and certain on the closing line.

lines.text: In June, federal, state and local agencies flew drones at a demonstration in Jim Wells County, South Texas. They were hunting a flesh-eating fly that is moving north over the border.
lines.intent: Setting the scene plainly, then naming the stakes
lines.note: Even and conversational. Weight falls on drones in the first sentence and on north in the second. Say Jim Wells County like a local, no lift on the place name. A small settle after border.

lines.text: The idea is simple. Drones, cameras and artificial intelligence could spot an injured or infested animal in country too rough to ride into. That is what the demonstration set out to show.
lines.intent: Explaining the premise without selling it
lines.note: Dry on simple, almost a shrug. Weight falls on rough. The last sentence drops a notch, matter of fact, as if the speaker is already a little skeptical.

lines.text: Michael Schmoyer of the USDA's animal health agency said the tools already work well on feral hogs. So the question was whether they could work on screwworm too.
lines.intent: Attribution, then the turn into the real question
lines.note: Name and title read flat and quick. Weight on hogs. The second sentence slows slightly and leans on screwworm, a plain question with no upward lilt at the end.

lines.text: Spotters in the air and on the ground will rely on cameras, infrared, night vision, heat sensors, dogs and AI. When a hide shows an open wound, the technology takes a closer look to see if the fly is attacking.
lines.intent: Walking through how the system works
lines.note: The list moves briskly with an even rhythm, a slight drop on the dogs so the animal is heard. Weight on open wound, said low and level. Closer look is practical, not dramatic.

lines.text: John Bellinger, a lead advisor to the Agriculture Secretary, has seen it before. He treated screwworm on calves at his grandfather's place in Wilson County. At the demonstration, he said it's back, and the country has to solve it.
lines.intent: Turning personal, a man who has lived this
lines.note: Warmer and a little slower than the list before. Weight on seen it before. Grandfather's place is said as a memory, softly. Its back lands flat and certain, with the weight on back.

lines.text: Spectrum News reported infected cases in Zavala, La Salle and Gillespie counties. The animals were cattle, a goat and a dog.
lines.intent: Laying down the facts, counted and unadorned
lines.note: Pull back to the plainest register in the piece so far. Counties read evenly, no emphasis on any one. Weight on dog, said quietly as the last item.

lines.text: Bellinger called wildlife one of the biggest challenges. White-tailed deer and feral hogs can become hosts without anyone knowing they were hurt.
lines.intent: Raising the hard part of the problem
lines.note: Weight on wildlife, then a slight slow down through the second sentence. Without anyone knowing is the heart of it, so leave it unhurried and let hurt land flat.

lines.text: So officials call technology one part of the plan. The most effective weapon, they say, is still the sterile fly program.
lines.intent: Deflating the gadget story, pointing at the old fix
lines.note: Dry, a touch wry on one part. Weight on still in the second sentence, which carries the whole turn. Land sterile fly program low and plain.

lines.text: Bellinger said the country needs 400 million sterile flies in 2027. As of June, a sterile fly plant in Edinburg was expected to open early that year.
lines.intent: Delivering the key figure and the timeline
lines.note: The quietest line in the piece, sitting on the most important fact. Say 400 million flat with no lift on million. Edinburg is read like a place the speaker knows. Early that year closes the line, level.

lines.text: USDA has help from Customs and Border Protection. KRGV reported that the drones use AI to flag animals that may be infected.
lines.intent: Adding a supporting detail and its source
lines.note: Brisk and informational, a small step up from the line before. Weight on help. KRGV is spelled out letter by letter, clean and quick. Flag is the verb to lean on.

lines.text: For now, producers are urged to inspect their animals more often and report any suspected case.
lines.intent: Giving the practical instruction to the people it concerns
lines.note: Speak directly to the rancher, plain and slower. Weight on inspect. Suspected case lands level, a clear instruction with nothing added.

lines.text: The drone can point. Somebody still has to walk out and look.
lines.intent: Landing the whole film on one dry, certain image
lines.note: Lowest and most certain delivery of the read. Point is short and flat. Then a full beat before the second sentence, with the weight on walk out and no rise on look.
